CHIEF COMPLAINT
Yearly exam

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
24-year-old female with history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension presenting for yearly examination. Patient reports feeling well overall. She began working at a bakery this summer and has enjoyed the position. However, due to close proximity to treats, she has been snacking frequently and consuming more desserts than usual during work shifts. She reports blood sugars have been up and down, which she attributes to dietary changes. Patient confirms she has been taking her medication as prescribed without missing doses. Blood pressure has been good despite fluctuations in blood glucose. She is sleeping well with approximately 8 hours of sleep per night. Denies safety concerns.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Otherwise unremarkable. Status quo except for diet-related issues discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, grade 2 systolic ejection murmur (unchanged)

MEDICATIONS
Metformin twice daily, Lisinopril 10 mg once daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works at a bakery, started this summer. Sleeps 8 hours per night.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Motor and sensory exam intact. Able to squeeze examiner's finger with good strength. Able to feel touch in extremities. Able to push and pull legs. Cardiovascular: Heart regular rate and rhythm with grade 2 systolic ejection murmur noted, unchanged from prior. Pulses good. No carotid bruits. Respiratory: Lungs clear. Extremities: No edema or swelling. Grip strength equal bilaterally. Neurovascular exam intact.

RESULTS
Hemoglobin A1c elevated. Blood pressure normal.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus – out of control
   - Goal hemoglobin A1c less than 7%, preferably less than 6%
   - Advised to reduce snacking and limit dessert intake
   - Instructed to check blood sugars in the morning
   - Patient to report fasting blood sugar in 2 weeks
   - Follow-up visit in 2 months to reassess
   - If not improved at follow-up, will consider adding additional medication
   - Continue metformin

2. Hypertension – stable
   - Continue lisinopril 10 mg once daily
   - No changes to current medication
